issues.display_title: Issue #27: Migration Binary — AI Image Gen
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Migration: ai-image-gen binary → native Rust

Migrate ai-image-gen.exe (source project: rust-image-staging) into the Tauri backend as in-process Rust, removing the external-process spawn used by virtual staging generate.

Branch (Development): migration/ai-image-gen-binary

Feasibility

Yes — the source is already pure Rust, and every runtime dep it needs (image, reqwest, base64, serde_json) is already in the backend. CLI-only deps (clap, indicatif, colored, gcp_auth) are not needed.

Scope

analyze and improve-description were already native (direct reqwest). Only generate still spawned the binary. Both spawn sites are now native:

Channel Was Now
room-staging-generate spawn ai-image-gen pano-edit --pipeline … ai_image_gen::run_pano_edit
virtual-staging-2d-generate spawn ai-image-gen --input … --image-type perspective ai_image_gen::run_generate_2d

New module src-tauri/src/ai_image_gen/: equirect.rs (warp/merge geometry, ported verbatim, now in-memory), strict.rs (prompt blocks — byte-identical text for output parity), providers.rs (Gemini + OpenAI, blocking reqwest), mod.rs (extract→AI→merge orchestration). Only the two paths the app used are ported; CLI-only modes (upscale, perspective, perspective-merge, single-step --boxes/--prompt, --extract-only, --rectilinear-from-equirect) are dropped.

Speed comparison (8000×4000 panorama, 1 region; native built --release)

The end-to-end generate is dominated by the AI network call (unchanged). Isolating the non-AI parts the migration changed:

Stage Binary (subprocess) Native (in-process)
Process spawn ~10 ms warm (~120 ms cold) eliminated
Extract (decode + warp) ~550 ms (writes max-compression PNG to disk) ~344 ms (in-memory)
Merge (32 MP) ~1425 ms (re-decodes from disk + re-encodes JPEG) ~724 ms (in-memory)
Geometry math only identical code identical
  • Geometry compute is the same algorithm/code → no algorithmic speedup.
  • Native removes per-call overhead: spawn, temp JSON/PNG/TXT writes, the extract-PNG disk round-trip between warp and the AI step, and redundant panorama decodes (~0.5–1.0 s per single-region generate, scaling with region count).
  • Also drops the ~8.8 MB binary from the bundle, removes the subprocess attack surface, leaves no temp files.

Follow-ups

  • Remove the now-unused ai-image-gen binary from repo + bundle config (verify tauri.conf.json first).
  • Update renderer dev-preview text in RoomStaging / VirtualStaging2D settings/utils/prompts.ts (cosmetic).### End-to-end parity test (real AI)
    Same input (1440×720 panorama), same 1-step pipeline, same key, same models (Gemini default gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview; OpenAI gpt-image-1). AI output is non-deterministic, so the check is functional parity (success/failure, preserved dimensions, comparable size).
Combo Binary Native Output dims Size (bin / native)
pano-edit · Gemini ✅ ✅ 1440×720 (= input) 232 / 235 KB
2D · Gemini ✅ ✅ 1440×720 (= input) 611 / 625 KB
pano-edit · OpenAI ✅ ✅ 1440×720 (= input) 229 / 229 KB
  • All four outcomes match. The three successes preserve the input dimensions exactly with near-identical sizes (delta = non-deterministic AI + JPEG q92).
  • 2D · OpenAI fails identically in both (error decoding response body: end of file) — pre-existing OpenAI /images/edits behavior (app feeds JPEG to a PNG-only endpoint), not a migration regression. The renderer always uses provider=google, so this path is parity-only.

End-to-end wall-clock (AI-dominated; large run-to-run variance at this small size): pano-edit·Gemini 14.6 s → 10.9 s · 2D·Gemini 11.5 s → 10.9 s · pano-edit·OpenAI 24.8 s → 28.7 s (binary → native). At 1440×720 the geometry/overhead delta (~0.5–1 s) is within AI jitter; it becomes visible at full 8000×4000 panoramas.

Note: the recorded installed-app evidence confirms the target app starts, the AI staging menu entries are visible, both generate functions are callable from the real app bridge, and validation/error handling works before provider execution. Live paid AI output generation was not re-run in this QA pass because no dedicated provider key/test fixture was supplied. The issue body already contains developer-run real-AI parity data for Gemini/OpenAI output outcomes.

Bug Notes / Follow-ups

  • Documentation drift: docs/migration/00-ipc-inventory.md and docs/migration/features/edit.md still classify the Room Staging / Virtual Staging 2D generate paths as sidecar, while source now uses native Rust. This can mislead future migration audits.
  • Cosmetic UI text drift: src/renderer/components/features/Edit/RoomStaging/settings/utils/prompts.ts and src/renderer/components/features/Edit/VirtualStaging2D/settings/utils/prompts.ts still say the generate flow runs the ai-image-gen binary.
  • Cleanup follow-up remains: the issue/doc notes src-tauri/binaries/win/ai-image-gen.exe and macOS binary are now unused and can be removed after bundle config verification.

Final QA Decision

Pass with follow-ups. The in-scope migration from ai-image-gen spawn to native Rust is wired correctly for both generate channels, compiles successfully, preserves renderer channel names, and both generate functions are callable in the installed real app with expected validation behavior. I am not claiming a fresh live-AI output parity run from this QA pass; that parity remains developer-documented in the issue body unless a provider key/fixture is supplied for tester rerun.

Result by developer

Migration: pano-level binary → native Rust (Issue #28)

Branch: `migration/pano-level-binary`

Summary

Migrates the bundled `pano-level.exe` (~31 MB, largest shipped binary) from an external process spawn to an in-process pure-Rust module. Implements the full HorizonNet `pano_lsd_align` algorithm in Rust.

Approach: Pure Rust (Approach A) — no C toolchain, no FFI, no OpenCV dependency.

Scope — Modules Ported

Rust file Source Responsibility
`pano_level/geometry.rs` geometry.cpp + types.hpp Vec2/Vec3/Mat3, trig, rodrigues, uv↔xyz
`pano_level/image_io.rs` image_io.cpp decode/encode, looks_equirectangular
`pano_level/projection.rs` pano_projection.cpp perspective tile extraction, ray↔pixel
`pano_level/lsd.rs` OpenCV lsd.cpp (Apache-2) Pure-Rust Line Segment Detector
`pano_level/detect.rs` line_detector.cpp per-tile LSD + spherical normals (rayon)
`pano_level/vp.rs` vp_estimator.cpp seeded RANSAC vertical VP + refine
`pano_level/confidence.rs` confidence.cpp confidence score + level
`pano_level/remap.rs` remap.cpp full-res panorama rotate (rayon bilinear)
`pano_level/mod.rs` leveling.cpp + main.cpp public API + pipeline orchestrator

Public API:

  • `level_panorama(input, output, opts) -> LevelReport` — apply leveling (Auto Level)
  • `estimate_metadata(input, opts) -> LevelReport` — dry-run, roll+pitch only (Image Straightener)

Integration — Call Sites Replaced

Call site Before After
`commands/auto_level.rs` `pano-level --input --output` spawn + pipe drain `pano_level::level_panorama()` direct call
`commands/binaries.rs::get_pano_level_metadata` `pano-level --dry-run --json -` spawn `pano_level::estimate_metadata()` via `spawn_blocking`

Both call sites: no more temp files, no pipe drain threads, no process exit code parsing.

Parity Bar

  • roll_deg / pitch_deg within ±0.1° of the binary on same panorama (tolerance, not bit-exact)
  • LSD is a reimplementation (pure Rust) — RANSAC weighted refine absorbs any segment-level differences
  • Apply output: same dimensions, visually equivalent leveling

Parity + Speed Results

Pending — run harness with real panoramas:

$env:PL_BIN="src-tauri/binaries/win/pano-level.exe"
$env:PL_PANOS="C:/path/a.jpg;C:/path/b.jpg"
cargo test --release --lib pano_level::validate -- --ignored --nocapture

Results doc: `docs/migration/pano-level-native-migration.md`

Key Technical Notes

  • LSD: Ported from OpenCV's Apache-2.0 `lsd.cpp` (not the original AGPL `lsd.c`). Found and fixed eigenvector bug during port: `atan2(λ₁ − mxx, mxy)` not `atan2(mxy, λ₁ − mxx)`.
  • RANSAC: `StdRng::seed_from_u64(1337)` (deterministic; not bit-identical to `mt19937(1337)`, absorbed by weighted refine).
  • Performance: rayon row-parallel remap + precomputed sin/cos tables; benchmark-driven JPEG encoder swap if encode-bound.
  • Cross-platform: Pure Rust, no platform-specific code → removes need for per-OS binaries.

Commits (12)

  • `7ba957e` feat(pano-level): scaffold module + geometry math port
  • `ba82267` feat(pano-level): image io + equirect check
  • `e0fe83f` feat(pano-level): perspective tile projection
  • `6e6cbf3` feat(pano-level): pure-Rust LSD line segment detector
  • `0029b88` feat(pano-level): per-tile spherical line detection

  • `3e43a9a` feat(pano-level): wire Image Straightener metadata to native
  • `17505bf` test(pano-level): parity + speed validation harness and results

QA Tester Summary - Issue #28: Migration Binary - pano-level

Suite: Pano-level native Rust migration audit + related feature wiring checks
Env: Local checkout qa-testing branch on Windows, 2026-07-07 10:22:11 +07:00
Scope: pano_level native Rust module, Auto Level batch apply path, Image Straightener metadata/roll-pitch path, installed-app visual evidence, migration docs

Test Scenario & Result

# Box Scenario Given -> Expected Matrix Result
1 White Native pano-level module and command registration pano_level exists and Tauri registers get_pano_level_metadata / Auto Level commands TP Pass
2 White Auto Level uses native Rust apply path Auto Level queue calls crate::pano_level::level_panorama() instead of spawning pano-level.exe TP Pass
3 Gray Image Straightener metadata uses native Rust estimate path Renderer getPanoLevelMetadata(imagePath) maps to Tauri get-pano-level-metadata, which calls estimate_metadata() in spawn_blocking TP Pass
4 Gray Documented dry-run parity Real pano dry-run result stays within +/-0.1 deg vs binary and native is not slower TP Pass, based on committed results doc
5 Gray Build and type safety Renderer build and TypeScript check complete TP Pass
6 Black Installed-app visual availability Installed Windows app launches and Edit UI is available for pano-level-related workflows TP Pass with screenshot/video evidence
7 Black Apply-mode output parity Native level_panorama() output should be validated against binary output dimensions/residual roll/pitch FN risk Not fully proven

Backend Status Code & Review

No HTTP backend endpoint is part of this issue. The migration surface is local Tauri/Rust command execution and filesystem image output.

Flow Contract Review
Image Straightener -> getPanoLevelMetadata Reads one image path and returns { success, roll, pitch } from native estimate_metadata() inside spawn_blocking; renderer applies returned roll/pitch to the manual leveling controls Verified by source inspection
Auto Level -> auto-level-start-queue Processes queued panorama paths, writes leveled output through native level_panorama(), then copies metadata with bundled exiftool Verified by source inspection
pano_level::validate harness Compares native dry-run roll/pitch and latency against pano-level.exe via PL_BIN + PL_PANOS Present, but not executed in this environment

Evidence

Check Result
npm.cmd run typecheck Pass
npm.cmd run build Pass, with existing Vite warnings for unresolved FontAwesome webfonts and large chunks
Installed app screenshot/video Pass; evidence uploaded to GitHub issue #28
where.exe cargo Failed: cargo is not installed/available in PATH
cargo test --release --lib pano_level::validate -- --ignored --nocapture Not run because Cargo is unavailable and no real PL_PANOS fixture path is configured

Findings

  • Blocking parity gap: Apply-mode parity is still not filled in docs/migration/pano-level-native-migration.md. The table remains a placeholder, so corrected-output dimensions/residual roll/pitch are not proven.
  • Tooling gap: The Rust parity harness cannot be executed on this machine until Cargo is available in PATH and a real panorama fixture is provided.
  • Documentation drift: docs/migration/pano-level-native-migration.md lists dependency image 0.24, while src-tauri/Cargo.toml currently uses image 0.25.
  • Documentation drift: docs/migration/00-ipc-inventory.md and docs/migration/features/edit.md still classify Auto Level / pano-level as sidecar, while current source calls crate::pano_level::level_panorama() and estimate_metadata() directly.

Conclusion

Scoped QA is partially passed for the binary-to-native-Rust migration. The related pano-level features are wired to the native Rust paths: Auto Level uses level_panorama() for apply mode, and Image Straightener uses estimate_metadata() to populate roll/pitch metadata. TypeScript, Vite build, and installed-app visual evidence pass. Final acceptance should remain open until the Rust parity harness is run with real panorama fixtures and apply-mode output parity is recorded.
